svg.title: Chains of Messages: Each Link Its Own Handling
svg.desc: A UML sequence diagram, read top to bottom, with six lifelines: the bus, Agent A, the Gate, Agent B, the agent MCP gateway and an outside system. The bus delivers a message to Agent A, which asks the Gate to decide; the Gate allows its action, and Agent A performs it: it publishes a message on the bus. The bus delivers that message to Agent B, which, a note says, acts for the same Principal. Agent B asks the Gate to decide on its own action, the Gate allows it, and Agent B performs its action through the agent MCP gateway, which calls the outside system, at most once. A note says each link is its own handling: checked, gated and recorded. Each Agent's handling performs one action, no Agent waits on another, and each Agent's lifeline is its agent runtime.
